questions.question: What is CSS Grid? Explain grid-template-columns, grid-template-rows, and grid-template-areas.
questions.title: CSS Grid Basics — Template Columns, Rows, Areas Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What is CSS Grid? Explain grid-template-columns, grid-template-rows, and grid-template-areas.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** 2D layout with explicit/implicit tracks; fr/minmax/repeat units; named areas for readable layouts; auto-placement.

**Classic weak answer:** Writing explicit positioning for every item when grid-template-areas and auto-placement would be cleaner.

**Senior finish:** Show a holy-grail layout in 5 lines with grid-template-areas; introduce subgrid (CSS Grid Level 2) for alignment across containers.

interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Show a holy-grail layout in 5 lines with grid-template-areas; introduce subgrid (CSS Grid Level 2) for alignment across containers

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **CSS Grid Basics — Template Columns, Rows, Areas Explained** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is CSS Grid? Explain grid-template-columns, grid-template-rows, and grid-template-areas.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **2D layout with explicit/implicit tracks; fr/minmax/repeat units; named areas for readable layouts; auto-placement**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Writing explicit positioning for every item when grid-template-areas and auto-placement would be cleaner**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show a holy-grail layout in 5 lines with grid-template-areas; introduce subgrid (CSS Grid Level 2) for alignment across containers**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** 2D layout with explicit/implicit tracks; fr/minmax/repeat units; named areas for readable layouts; auto-placement
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **writing explicit positioning for every item when grid-template-areas and auto-placement would be cleaner** and what you do instead.

questions.question: Flexbox vs CSS Grid — when should you use each?
questions.title: Flexbox vs CSS Grid — Differences and When to Use Each
questions.direct_answer:
Flexbox vs CSS Grid — when should you use each?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Flexbox is 1D (row OR column), Grid is 2D (rows AND columns); Grid for page layout, Flexbox for component-level alignment; they combine well.

**Classic weak answer:** Treating it as either/or — most real layouts combine Grid (page) with Flexbox (card contents).

**Senior finish:** Rule of thumb: Grid for where things go in 2D space; Flexbox for distribution along one axis; gap works in both.
